arxiv-2210-10474.title: Video super-resolution for single-photon LIDAR
arxiv-2210-10474.creator: Germán Mora Martín, Stirling Scholes, Alice Ruget, Robert K. Henderson, Jonathan Leach, Istvan Gyongy
arxiv-2210-10474.description: Abstract 3D Time-of-Flight (ToF) image sensors are used widely in applications such as self-driving cars, Augmented Reality (AR) and robotics. When implemented with Single-Photon Avalanche Diodes (SPADs), compact, array format sensors can be made that offer accurate depth maps over long distances, without the need for mechanical scanning.

arxiv-2406-03666.title: What Makes Language Models Good-enough?
arxiv-2406-03666.creator: Daiki Asami, Saku Sugawara
arxiv-2406-03666.description: Abstract Psycholinguistic research suggests that humans may build a representation of linguistic input that is ‘good-enough’ for the task at hand. This study examines what architectural features make language models learn human-like good-enough language processing. We focus on the number of layers and self-attention heads in Transformers.

arxiv-2506-20008.title: QHackBench: Benchmarking Large Language Models for Quantum Code Generation Using PennyLane Hackathon Challenges
arxiv-2506-20008.creator: Abdul Basit 1 , Minghao Shao 1 , Haider Asif 1,2 , Nouhaila Innan 1,2 , Muhammad Kashif 1,2 , Alberto Marchisio 1,2 , Muhammad Shafique 1,2
arxiv-2506-20008.description: Abstract Recent advances in Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong potential in code generation, yet their effectiveness in quantum computing remains underexplored. This paper benchmarks LLMs for PennyLane-based quantum code generation using real-world challenges from the Quantum Hackathon (QHack).

arxiv-2508-18113.title: The AI Data Scientist Publication type: Article Journal: arXiv preprint Volume: 00
arxiv-2508-18113.creator: Farkhad Akimov, Munachiso Samuel Nwadike, Zangir Iklassov, Martin Takáč
arxiv-2508-18113.description: Abstract Imagine decision-makers uploading data and, within minutes, receiving clear, actionable insights delivered straight to their fingertips. That is the promise of the AI Data Scientist, an autonomous Agent powered by large language models (LLMs) that closes the gap between evidence and action.

pmc-11370226.title: Congenital myopathies: pathophysiological mechanisms and promising therapies
pmc-11370226.creator: Han Zhang, Mengyuan Chang, Daiyue Chen, Jiawen Yang, Yijie Zhang, Jiacheng Sun, Xinlei Yao, Hualin Sun, Xiaosong Gu, Meiyuan Li, Yuntian Shen, Bin Dai
pmc-11370226.description: Congenital myopathies (CMs) are a kind of non-progressive or slow-progressive muscle diseases caused by genetic mutations, which are currently defined and categorized mainly according to their clinicopathological features. CMs exhibit pleiotropy and genetic heterogeneity. Currently, supportive treatment and pharmacological remission are the mainstay of treatment, with no cure available.

pmc-11402613.title: Case of pulmonary Langerhans cell histiocytosis presenting as ground-glass opacity in the lower lung
pmc-11402613.creator: Hong Lyeol Lee, Lucia Kim, Kyung Hee Lee, Cheol-Woo Kim
pmc-11402613.description: Nodules and cysts with upper lobe predominance on chest computed tomography (CT) are highly suggestive of pulmonary Langerhans cell histiocytosis (PLCH). Herein, we describe a case of PLCH that presented with the unusual CT findings of subpleural ground-glass opacity (GGO) and traction bronchiectasis mostly in both lower lungs.

pmc-11457329.title: Quantifying the magnitude of the general contextual effect in a multilevel study of SARS-CoV-2 infection in Ontario, Canada: application of the median rate ratio in population health research
pmc-11457329.creator: Tristan Watson, Jeffrey C. Kwong, Kathy Kornas, Sharmistha Mishra, Laura C. Rosella
pmc-11457329.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundRegional variations in SARS-CoV-2 infection were observed in Canada and other countries. Studies have used multilevel analyses to examine how a context, such as a neighbourhood, can affect the SARS-CoV-2 infection rates of the people within it. However, few multilevel studies have quantified the magnitude of the general contextual effect (GCE) in SARS-CoV-2 infection rates and assessed how it may be associated with individual- and area-level characteristics.

pmc-11520809.title: MAKO robot-assisted total hip arthroplasty: a comprehensive meta-analysis of efficacy and safety outcomes
pmc-11520809.creator: Rafael Llombart-Blanco, Gonzalo Mariscal, Carlos Barrios, Pablo Vera, Rafael Llombart-Ais
pmc-11520809.description: BackgroundIntroduction: Robotic surgery in total hip arthroplasty (THA) has emerged as a promising approach for improving precision and reducing errors. This meta-analysis aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of robot-assisted MAKO total hip arthroplasty.MethodsStudies were searched using four databases. Meta-analysis was performed using Review Manager 5.4. Efficacy was assessed radiologically, and functional scores and complications were recorded.

pmc-12568187.title: Serological Response to COVID-19 Vaccination in Saudi Arabia: A Comparative Study of IgG and Neutralising Antibodies Across Vaccine Platforms
pmc-12568187.creator: Mariam M AlEissa, Ahdab A Alsaieedi, Reema Alduaiji, Fahad Almsned, Yousif AlDossary, Nada Saleh, Raghad A AlQurashi, Esraa A Hawsa, Muath b Ben Shaded, Amer M Alshehri, Osamah T Khojah, Eyad Y Abu Sarhan, Hamad H Alonazi, Walid A Nouh, Khalid H AlAnazi, Sami S Almudrra, Khaled I AlAbdulkareem, Abdu
pmc-12568187.description: Background: In the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, various COVID-19 vaccines were administered during the pandemic. However, region-specific real-word comparative data on their immunogenicity remain limited. This study aimed to assess the serological responses to Pfizer-BioNTech (BNT162b2), Moderna (mRNA-1273), and AstraZeneca (ChAdOx1 nCoV-19) vaccines in a diverse population living in KSA.

pmc-12581432.title: Aberrant hippocampal gamma oscillations in a mouse model of fragile X syndrome: insights from in vitro slice models
pmc-12581432.creator: Evangelia Pollali, Daniel Frías Donaire, Miguel Del Ángel, Yunus Emre Demiray, Sara Enrile Lacalle, Jan-Oliver Hollnagel, Anil Annamneedi, Gürsel Çalışkan
pmc-12581432.description: BackgroundFragile X syndrome (FXS) is the most common inherited intellectual disability, caused by the loss of fragile X mental retardation protein (FMRP), which regulates neuronal signaling and plasticity. FXS patients and Fmr1 knockout (KO) mice exhibit sensory hypersensitivity, hyperarousal, and hippocampus-dependent learning deficits.

pmc-13015031.title: ‘Being empathetic to my patients and ourselves’: a qualitative process evaluation of READ-Y psychological first aid training for healthcare workers working in routine care
pmc-13015031.creator: Ling Wang, Xizhao Li, Cailiang Qiu, Jianjian Wang, Lina Zeng, Ting Liu, Ziqing Zhong, Yeqing Wu, Lin Xu, Yuping Liu, Mary Leamy, Muli Hu
pmc-13015031.description: Introduction: Healthcare workers (HCWs) are routinely exposed to distressing and potentially traumatic events during frontline care, yet receive limited structure training to manage such exposure. Psychological first aid (PFA) training has been widely disseminated among emergency responders and is increasingly being adapted for HCWs; however, its acceptability, implementation, and use in routine care remain underexplored.

pmc-13250430.title: Arthroscopic Conjoint Tendon Release for Painful Reverse Total Shoulder Arthroplasty
pmc-13250430.creator: Katherine A Burns, Jocelyn R Wittstein, Jennifer Beck, Claudia Arias, Camille Coates-Clark
pmc-13250430.description: Background:Persistent pain after reverse total shoulder arthroplasty (RTSA) is a difficult problem to manage. Anterior shoulder pain may arise from conditions, including anterior impingement, conjoint tendonitis, or coracoid fracture after RTSA. Clinical function and anterior pain may improve after release of the conjoint tendon. An open technique for conjoint tendon release has been described.

pmc-13285551.title: TAX1BP1 targets STING1 via microautophagy and Golgiphagy to limit inflammatory signaling
pmc-13285551.creator: Sujit Suklabaidya, Suchitra Mohanty, Edward W Harhaj
pmc-13285551.description: The CGAS-STING1 pathway plays a key role in detecting cytosolic DNA and initiating immune responses. Excessive STING1 activation can lead to aberrant inflammation and autoinflammatory diseases; therefore, the STING1 degradation pathway is tightly regulated by several negative regulatory mechanisms. In our recent study, we show that the selective autophagy receptor TAX1BP1 functions as a negative regulator of STING1 signaling.

pmc-13295491.creator: Barlina Konwar, Kwang-sun Kim

pmc-13326490.title: IRE1/p‑JNK/NRF2 axis-mediated GPX4 upregulation underlies ferroptosis resistance in rheumatoid arthritis fibroblast-like synoviocytes
pmc-13326490.creator: Jiaxi Liu, Wenhui Xie, Yongping Cao, Liang Zhang, Yan Geng, Zhuoli Zhang
pmc-13326490.description: BackgroundRheumatoid arthritis fibroblast‑like synoviocytes (RA‑FLS) exhibit chronic endoplasmic reticulum stress with activation of the IRE1/phospho‑JNK arm of the unfolded protein response; yet, they remain resistant to apoptosis. Although ferroptosis has been implicated in the pathogenesis of rheumatoid arthritis, the mechanisms underlying ferroptosis resistance in RA‑FLS remain poorly understood.

pmc-13327602.title: Engineering human peritoneum in vitro: A novel microfluidic platform for modeling peritoneal physiology and pathophysiology
pmc-13327602.creator: Katharina Peisert, Franziska Keßler, Sara Y Brucker, Jan Pauluschke‐Fröhlich, Peter Jakubowski, Felix Neis, Bernhard Krämer, Jürgen Andress, Adrian Weghofer, Hui‐Yu Liu, Peter Loskill, Martin Weiss
pmc-13327602.description: The peritoneum, the body's largest serous membrane, plays critical roles in abdominal homeostasis and immune defense. When disrupted by surgery or disease, it can lead to devastating complications including peritoneal adhesions—affecting up to 93% of surgical patients—peritonitis, and metastatic spread.

pmc-13454274.title: Ethnoveterinary medicinal plants in Aseko District, Arsi Zone, southeastern Ethiopia
pmc-13454274.creator: Jewar Safeno Jara, Melesse Maryo, Zerihun Girma
pmc-13454274.description: Ethnoveterinary medicine remains a key component of livestock healthcare in rural Ethiopia, particularly in areas with limited access to modern veterinary services. This study documented ethnoveterinary medicinal plants, associated indigenous knowledge systems, and conservation challenges in Aseko District, Arsi Zone, southeastern Ethiopia, using a bilingual (English–Afaan Oromo) disease classification framework to improve diagnostic clarity and strengthen veterinary relevance.

uslaw-usc-t22-s4705.title: 22 U.S.C. § 4705 — Authority to enter into agreements
uslaw-usc-t22-s4705.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t22-s4705.description: United States Code, Title 22 (Foreign Relations And Intercourse); Chapter 57 (United States Scholarship Program For Developing Countries). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. The President may enter into agreements with foreign governments in furtherance of the purposes of this chapter. Such agreements may provide for the creation or continuation of binational or multinational educational and cultural foundations and commissions for the purposes.

uslaw-usc-t34-s10703.title: 34 U.S.C. § 10703 — Review of applications
uslaw-usc-t34-s10703.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t34-s10703.description: United States Code, Title 34 (Crime Control And Law Enforcement); Chapter 101 (Justice System Improvement); Subchapter XXXVIII (Comprehensive Opioid Abuse Grant Program). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. The Attorney General shall not finally disapprove any application (or any amendment to that application) submitted under this subchapter without first affording the applicant reasonable notice of any deficiencies in the application and an opportunity.

uslaw-usc-t42-s12753.title: 42 U.S.C. § 12753 — Program enforcement and penalties for noncompliance
uslaw-usc-t42-s12753.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t42-s12753.description: United States Code, Title 42 (The Public Health And Welfare); Chapter 130 (National Affordable Housing); Subchapter II (Investment In Affordable Housing); Part A (Home Investment Partnerships). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. If the Secretary finds after reasonable notice and opportunity for hearing that a participating jurisdiction has failed to comply substantially with any provision of this part, including any provision applicable throughout.
